security_spec.violation_condition: The kernel extracts the interrupt identifier from scause by masking with ~CAUSE_IRQ_FLAG and using the full remaining XLEN-1 bits as a flat interrupt number (e.g., in riscv_intc_irq at drivers/irqchip/irq-riscv-intc.c:31). Under Smivt/CLIC with stvec.MODE=11, external interrupts encode Major Interrupt Identity in bits 15:0 and Minor Interrupt Identity in bits XLEN-2:16 of xcause, producing a corrupted composite value when parsed with the standard flat-numbering mask. The kernel also uses raw scause values to index the excp_vect_table in entry.S by left-shifting the full scause value, which would compute a wildly incorrect table offset if scause were in CLIC format. Any code path where the kernel or KVM host sets stvec.MODE=11 without corresponding updates to scause parsing triggers this mismatch.
security_spec.summary: CLIC Smivt repurposes scause exception code field when stvec.MODE=11 for external interrupts, splitting into major[15:0]/minor[XLEN-2:16] identity; kernel scause parsing assumes unpartitioned flat interrupt numbering and would yield garbage hwirq values and incorrect trap dispatching.

findings.finding: Uses the standard flat-numbering mask `cause & ~CAUSE_IRQ_FLAG` to extract the interrupt identifier from scause. Under Smivt/CLIC with stvec.MODE=11, external interrupts encode Major Interrupt Identity in bits 15:0 and Minor Interrupt Identity in bits XLEN-2:16 of xcause, so this mask would produce a corrupted composite value. Currently no kernel code sets stvec.MODE=11 — stvec is always configured to direct mode (MODE=00) via `csrw CSR_TVEC, handle_exception` in head.S:206 — so this is latent and not actively triggerable. However, if firmware or a hypervisor were to enable CLIC vectoring mode, or if the kernel adds Smivt support without updating this parsing, the interrupt handler would misidentify interrupts, leading to denial of service.

When AIA (SxAIA) is available, the kernel uses riscv_intc_aia_irq() which reads from the TOPI CSR instead of parsing scause with the flat-numbering mask. TOPI-based interrupt identification is correct regardless of stvec mode, so this path would be immune to the Smivt/CLIC parsing mismatch. The vulnerable riscv_intc_irq() is only selected when AIA is absent.

The excp_vect_table indexing via `slli t0, s4, RISCV_LGPTR` left-shifts the full scause value to compute a table offset. This code is only reached for exceptions (non-interrupts), guarded by `bge s4, zero, 1f` at line 218 which branches to the IRQ handler for interrupts. Under CLIC, exception cause values remain in standard Privileged Architecture encoding — only interrupt causes are in CLIC format. Therefore this table lookup is not affected by Smivt/CLIC.
findings.snippet:
slli t0, s4, RISCV_LGPTR
la t1, excp_vect_table
la t2, excp_vect_table_end
add t0, t1, t0
bgeu t0, t2, 3f
REG_L t1, 0(t0)

findings.finding: The raw scause value (s4 from CSR_CAUSE) is stored verbatim into pt_regs->cause at PT_CAUSE(sp). This raw value is later consumed by riscv_intc_irq() which applies the `& ~CAUSE_IRQ_FLAG` flat-numbering mask. Under CLIC MODE=11, the raw scause for external interrupts would contain the composite Major/Minor identity encoding rather than a flat interrupt number. However, the kernel does not set MODE=11, so this is currently latent. The MSB check at line 218 (`bge s4, zero, 1f`) for distinguishing interrupts from exceptions remains correct under CLIC since the MSB still carries the interrupt/exception flag.
findings.snippet:
csrr s4, CSR_CAUSE
csrr s5, CSR_SCRATCH
REG_S s0, PT_SP(sp)
REG_S s1, PT_STATUS(sp)
REG_S s2, PT_EPC(sp)
REG_S s3, PT_BADADDR(sp)
REG_S s4, PT_CAUSE(sp)

findings.finding: The IRQ flag check `trap->scause & CAUSE_IRQ_FLAG` only tests the MSB to distinguish host interrupts from guest traps. Under CLIC encoding, the MSB still serves as the interrupt/exception flag, so this check is correct regardless of stvec mode. The KVM host's own stvec is set to `__kvm_riscv_unpriv_trap` (direct mode) during unpriv reads, and the host kernel stvec is always in direct mode, so scause on VM exit is never in CLIC format from the host side.

KVM temporarily redirects stvec to `__kvm_riscv_unpriv_trap` (a direct-mode address, MODE=00) for HLV/HLVX guest memory access emulation. Both the saved old_stvec and the temporary stvec are direct-mode values. The stvec swap is properly restored at line 125. No MODE=11 is ever set, so scause values during this window remain in flat format.

KVM reads scause via `csr_read(CSR_SCAUSE)` at VM exit. Since the KVM host's stvec is in direct mode (MODE=00), the scause value on VM exit is always in standard flat format, not CLIC format. The VM exit occurs because the host took the interrupt, so scause reflects the host-side cause. Even if the guest internally used CLIC vectoring, the VM exit would still present a host-formatted scause.

The kernel trap vector is configured to direct mode by writing `handle_exception` address directly to CSR_TVEC (stvec). No MODE bits are set — the address of handle_exception is naturally aligned to at least 4 bytes, so bits 1:0 of stvec are 0, meaning MODE=00 (Direct). This is the only place where stvec is configured for normal kernel operation, confirming the kernel never enables CLIC vectoring mode.
findings.snippet:
.Lsetup_trap_vector:
	/* Set trap vector to exception handler */
	la a0, handle_exception
	csrw CSR_TVEC, a0
